<section class="research-introduction" aria-label="Research overview"><h2>Research overview</h2><p>My research lies at the interface of atomic physics, low-temperature plasma science, and optical diagnostics, with a focus on building a quantitative understanding of non-equilibrium plasmas and translating that understanding into applications. Our group combines experiments and computation to study plasma sources, electron–atom collision processes, and population kinetics, and we develop collisional-radiative models that link the light emitted by a plasma to its underlying parameters. We have integrated machine learning with these models to enable fast, reliable optical diagnostics. We have recently begun investigating quantum algorithm-based frameworks for plasma physics problems, exploring how emerging quantum computing approaches can complement conventional methods. Alongside this fundamental work, we explore plasma-based technologies for environmental treatment, food safety, and agriculture, aiming to connect basic plasma physics with solutions to real-world problems.</p></section>
